Daily Devotional

October 6

16 Wherefore henceforth know we no man after the flesh: yea, though we have known Christ after the flesh, yet now henceforth know we him no more. (2 Corinthians 5:16 KJV)

Paul is writing this, and I am sure he had seen Jesus in the flesh as Jesus taught in Jerusalem many times. We, as Christians, should not know people, or judge them, by the flesh, but should always try to see their spirits. This is what Paul is saying in this verse, that although he had known Jesus in the flesh, he now only knew Him in the spirit. Jesus own disciples, who walked for years with Him, knew Him by the flesh real well, but had a hard time trying to know Him by the spirit.

Most of us Christians would have thought it wonderful to have been alive in the days of Jesus, and been able to walk and talk with Him. But we are truly more blessed to be living in this day with the Scriptures that we have, and all the knowledge we have on what Jesus was like, and what He accomplished for us. Seeing Jesus in the flesh would have made it hard to realize that it was God in the flesh (John 1:1) that we were looking at. After all, even though Jesus was God, His body was just completely normal, and He did not look special (Isaiah 53:2), and it would have been hard to look at Him and think – This is God? Remember, that He was all human, as well as all God, and had to go to the bathroom, get sweaty and stink, etc. You know that His hair got messed up, and He got dirty, as they had to walk everywhere in the hot sun. They didn’t have motels to stay in, and couldn’t shower every day like we do. Wow – when you think of those things, how hard would it have been to think that He was God in the flesh? Thank you Lord for your Word!

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com

Debt relief history

If a debt cannot be or is not repaid, alternatives that were common historically but are now rare include debt bondage – including debt peonage: being bound until the debt is repaid; and debt slavery, when the debt is so great (or labor valued so low) that the debt will never be repaid – and debtors' prison.

Debt slavery can persist across generations, future generations being made to work to pay off debts incurred by past generations. Debt bondage is today considered a form of "modern day slavery" in international law, and banned as such, in Article 1(a) of the United Nations 1956 Supplementary Convention on the Abolition of Slavery. Nevertheless, the practice continues in some nations. In most developed nations, debts cannot be inherited.

Debtors' prison has been largely abolished, but remains in some forms in the US, for example if one fails to make child support payments.
